missing: Engagement, pracinostat-mouse-xenograft track: Mol Cancer Ther 2011 tissue-acH3 PD paper (doi 10.1158/1535-7163.mct-11-0044, PMID 21586629, epub 2011-05-17) is a stated comparison the draft lacks: acH3 tracked SB939 dose in HCT-116 xenograft and HL-60 orthotopic SCID tissues (r2 0.76-0.94), then rose dose-dependently (10-80 mg) in PBMCs of 30 solid-tumour phase 1 patients (r=0.97 with Cmax/AUC); the abstract states the PK/PD 'are translated from preclinical models to patients'. A 2011 same, comparison_stated true, subjects patients (solid tumour; decision 3 admits any subjects for engagement), ahead of the adjudicated 2017 Abaza same; whether the 2017 same+partial entry remains a status change under decision 7 is the adjudicator's call.

Engagement, panobinostat-leukemia-cells track: Int J Oncol 2014 (doi 10.3892/ijo.2014.2555, PMID 25051119, epub 2014-07-22) compares HL-60 cells treated with azacitidine plus panobinostat (caspase-3, Nor-1, NUR77, p15, p21 up; Bcl-xL down) with PBMCs from the Tan 2014 phase Ib/II: NUR77 and p21 rose after cycle 1 and more in responders than non-responders. Makes the 2014 Tan entry a stated comparison (comparison_stated true, this paper as src or model_src) instead of a drafter pairing; the checker's Giles 2006 re-dating still sets the track's first comparison.

Engagement, panobinostat-leukemia-cells x panobinostat x iv: Giles 2006 (PMID 16899611) H3/H2B acetylation rose in CD34+ blasts of IV-dosed AML/MDS patients; an IV engagement track (retro, 2006) is absent now that the oral entry is re-dated to its own route.
checker_notes: No model compared with MDS patients for any member was found. Candidates checked and rejected: ATF3 as marker of pracinostat response (MCT 2016, 10.1158/1535-7163.mct-15-0890; solid-tumour cells, no MDS patient comparison); ex vivo synergy screening in hematologic malignancies (SLAS Discov 2024, 10.1016/j.slasd.2023.12.001; no patient-outcome comparison for this class, post-result); PDX MDS/AML azacitidine-venetoclax resistance (Front Oncol 2024; panobinostat not the subject).
Ivaltinostat/CG200745: 19 title hits, all solid tumour, fibrosis or kidney models; no AML/MDS model, no results for NCT02737462 (status UNKNOWN). 'No track' is right.

Press/registry sweep: Helsinn/MEI 2020-07-02 release confirms PRIMULA (NCT03151408, AML) futility stop; the MDS 45 mg phase 2 was then ongoing and later terminated by sponsor (registry). No MDS failure is missing from the draft.

Abstract-level reads: Novotny-Diermayr 2010, Jayaraman 2011, Giles 2006, Fiskus 2009 (quotes are in the abstracts). Full text read: Abaza 2017 (PMC5901648), Dimicoli 2012 (PMC4085038), FDA PharmR 205353.

Minor: the engagement-2 judgement says the trial papers do not cite the mouse PD data; Abaza 2017 does (ref 10). Registry calls the PRIMULA stop 'lack of efficacy'; the press release calls it an interim futility analysis.

Models pass (CHECKER_BRIEF_v3 / models): lint 0 findings on the merged draft. After the re-key, xenograft dose 3 (Garcia-Manero 2017, derived contra) still names Jayaraman 2011 (10.1124/dmd.111.041558) as model_src, which now belongs to pracinostat-allometry-simcyp-pk; its model side should be the track's own opener, Novotny-Diermayr 2010 (10.1158/1535-7163.MCT-09-0689). Dose 2's judgement ('the 2017 entry then records that reaching it did not translate') now points off-track too. The xenograft dose cell itself (untested 2010 -> derived contra 2017: 60 mg RP2D delivered, randomized primary failed, regimen abandoned) stays coherent, since decision 4 case 3 does not rest on the PK match. Ivaltinostat: no model, no track, agreed.
rule_questions: Engagement: the model predicted an exposure-dependent readout (sustained, dose-dependent AcH3 in mice) and patients showed the readout moving without dose dependence (Abaza 2017). Decision 4 reads 'moved' = same, decision 11 makes it partial; the drafter read the lost dose-dependence as contra. Which is decided?

Dose: the protocol dose (60 mg RP2D) was delivered and the trial failed, but the sponsor attributes failure to toxicity-driven early discontinuation (sub-optimal cumulative exposure) and the model stated no margin (efficacy at the mouse MTD). Decision 4 case 3 (derived contra) or decision 16 (untested, no stated margin)?
Dose on an ex vivo cell track that stated no exposure or occupancy target: is 'reached' definable, so case 3 derived contra applies, or is the cell untested?

Model identity: a human PK prediction from mouse/rat/dog allometry plus Simcyp (Jayaraman 2011) sits on the mouse-xenograft model_id. Decision 8 says any system the class relied on counts, labelled; is multi-species PK scaling the same track as the xenograft efficacy model or its own?

Safety: animal findings the label says were 'not reported (or reported with low incidence)' in patients, where the AE tables do list them at low incidence. Decision 11 (right hazard, wrong incidence, same) rather than decision 5 (never came, contra)? And one entry same+partial, or one entry per harm, when a single package matches one harm and over-predicts another?

Efficacy: a randomized phase 2b whose primary endpoint (composite CR 27.5% vs 14.3%) was numerically higher with overlapping CIs, no OS/TTP difference, and the sponsor abandoned the regimen. Does it add a same+partial entry on a track already contra, or change nothing?

Dating: the earliest patient comparison (Giles 2006) predates the drafter's chosen model paper (Fiskus 2009) but follows the system's first use (George 2004). Rule 6/decision 7 is read here as opening the track at 2004 and dating the comparison 2006; confirm that the opener follows the system, not the paper the drafter picked.

In-silico PK prediction whose run date is not public (Jayaraman 2011): the published predicted-vs-observed comparison (epub 2011-08) postdates the phase 1 PK reports (2011-02/03) and the 2007 FIH, but IND-enabling allometry/Simcyp ordinarily precedes FIH. Decision 10 requires 'post-dates and is motivated by the patient result'; scored retro here for consistency with famitinib-pbpk-rat-monkey-human-pk. Does an unverifiable run date default to retro, or does an IND-enabling presumption give same?

Safety on a mixed hematologic phase 1 (13 AML, 1 ALL, 1 MDS) when MDS patients were measured on another route of the same drug: is the IV track's comparison other_disease (as proposed) and still scored, or untested (unsettled) because the MDS-only result is not separable?
